scenes.b: Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya…

The Himalayas… those mighty peaks… In their lap, sages have performed tapas for ages. Ancient tales say — their very penance is the foundation of this earth. Their silence became a mantra for the world… and blessed it anew.
In that age, the forests were filled with sounds… yet no sound was ever without meaning. Every leaf swayed with breath… every river flowed toward wisdom. In such forests… our story is being born.
On that riverbank… man lived simply and lovingly like the creatures — a little world. No walls to walk within… no watchman either. That world's name — the ashrama.

Five little huts… one great banyan tree… beneath its shade, a seat… and around it, a daily yajna of knowledge. Here dwells the great sage of this age… Vyasa Maharshi. This earth honors him deeply… people of every land take refuge in his name.
Beneath that banyan… he sat.

Every morning begins just like this. The disciples come… bow… and behold the light on the sage's face. To them, he is not a Guru… he is the dawn itself. Among the disciples — Paila, Jaimini, Vaishampayana, Sumantu… and the youngest, Gurudatta.

Every lesson he taught… like a seed cast into the river… spread into people's lives. Veda, Purana, dharma, love — whatever his lips touched turned to nectar. But mark this — however much he taught, the letter of ego never entered his words.

On all those nights when the forest slept, this sage, with this very hand… poured letters onto the page. How much did he write? Ask, and the legends reply — can you count the waters of the Ganga? So great a writer… so selfless a doer.

A single Veda… he divided into four paths. Rig Veda… Yajur Veda… Sama Veda… Atharva Veda. And so he earned the name — Veda Vyasa. The Divider. History tells us the same hand wrote the Mahabharata too. But one thing he could not divide… his own heart.

Tapas, he used to say, is not hardship. Tapas is — the holding still of the mind. In a stilled mind, knowledge alone is reflected. For such a man, why would the mind refuse to be still? This question was known to no one. Only to him.
Through the voices of his disciples… the Veda flowed on as sound. Hearing it, he smiled — knowing his breath lived on in other throats. But no one noticed… that smile no longer smiled fully.

In those days, sages from far lands came on foot… to resolve a single doubt. The whole world believed — he holds the answer. That faith was his throne. They crossed mountains… deep forests… walked for months on that one hope.
Simply to behold him was counted a blessing. Children gazed with fresh eyes… the old remembered those eyes forever. In everyone's eyes, he was complete. No lack appeared on anyone's face.
Evening falls. Everyone returns home… talking of him, of his greatness…
All day, a light lives in his eyes — because everyone is watching.

The scriptures he had written lay heaped through the house. His hand… not with weariness but with bewilderment… with an immeasurable weight… slowly rested upon the bundles. All night the wind hummed outside… inside, only silence.
The lamp flame — turned within his eyes.
At night… he came to the river. He had no habit of speaking to it. But the river, never questioning, flowed on listening with patience. Yet tonight, even that patient voice… did not reach his heart.
The reflection in the water — so majestic. But let one small drop fall… and everything trembles.
That night… in his hands, countless scriptures… in his mind, immeasurable knowledge… before his eyes, countless stars.
Another morning came. Whatever lay within stayed hidden from all… but the ashrama's daily face remained the same — peace, discipline, dharma. That was its beauty… that was its vow.

Fetching water, here, too, is tapas. Little Gurudatta carries a little pot — for growing strength, that itself is his great practice. Descending the steps, the disciples pour prayers along with the water.
Having done good deeds since morning, in the midday lesson, young Gurudatta's eyes became a little of the earth's. That weariness was no fault… only a child's sleep.
Agnihotra — the temple of the forest. With this sacred fire, all here have been familiar since childhood. Before the fire, the mind is purified — that is what he himself had taught.
But today… in the teacher's own heart… is it only fire that burns? Fire knows everything… perchance it may reveal the heart's secret to the Maharshi.

In the ashrama, not only humans… every living creature looked with eyes of grace. Here, the forest is unafraid — no one troubles anyone. Sometimes even monkeys arrive like guests… and leave within moments.

Every small task of the ashrama is a vow. Sweeping, sprinkling, carrying wood — all owe one debt: to have given this world something by day's end. But in the heart of that family's eldest… no task takes shape today.

If a disciple erred, he called it a mistake of learning. If the disciple felt shame, he laid a hand on his shoulder. For he was not one who merely gave knowledge — he grew it. With such a Guru, even to err is a fortune.
The hour of evening aarti — every heart sways in one rhythm. In those moments, the ashrama looks like a little Vaikuntha. Humility, peace, completeness — all merged into a single lamp.
At night, the ashrama's lamps go out one by one. The ashrama sleeps like a child.
If the home's lamp is this small… then the darkness is that vast.
Another morning… another leaf… another inkwell. All is ready — but today, the hand has stopped. Not because there is no scripture to write…
Look at this river… it is full. Yet it does not stop. Do you know why? It knows — until I reach the ocean… being full is not enough.
His hand rested upon his chest. There was no lack of knowledge there. No lack of devotion. But… an emptiness — a vacancy not yet named.
Until yesterday… around him was the world. But today…
That day, for the first time… some words came out of the Maharshi's mouth. Not for anyone to hear…
However vast the sky may be… greater still is a single human question.
Look at that monkey… even it knows the ashrama's way — everything there has its place. However great one may be, before one little monkey this world cannot stand still.
That smile… how much longer will it remain upon his face?
About their Gurudev's heart… the disciples themselves convened a scholarly assembly — see for yourselves. To them, the Guru is divine — and they could not believe that the divine may feel sorrow.
The disciples' words stayed with them. But Gurudev's steps… along the river… continued as though searching for something.
In the forest, the footsteps grew deeper. The trees grew taller.
Beneath the ashrama's banyan… he used to teach them all.
He closed his eyes. To see what lay within.
He opened his eyes. The river was flowing just the same.
He touched that bundle. In that bundle… there are only palm leaves.
Monsoons came… and went. Springs came… and went.
Spring did not come within. Only the wind came. And in that wind… that question… again.
He asked the question. The answer… did not come.
Then…
Suddenly…
In the ashrama too… change had arrived.
Then… in the wind…
Through the trees… a light was walking toward them…
The disciples gathered at the gate.
The Maharshi… walked toward the gate.
Those steps… halted on the ashrama's stairs.
Narayana… Narayana… Narayana…
Upon the shoulder, the Mahati veena. Upon the chest, a garland of pearls. Upon the body, white silk.
Narada Maharshi.
The disciples bowed. Because they knew who he was.
Gurudev arrived.
Two great sages… in a single courtyard… in a single breath of air… stood.
Narada's smile… drawing nearer.

Salutations, O Maharshi. Vyasa Maharshi. … To the question that had lived for years in Vyasa Maharshi's heart — the answer comes in the next part… Having written everything… why was there still no peace?
